LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: PARAGRAPH WRITING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Writing 3.2 Guided Writing: Neatness and Legibility (2 Sessions) • Handwriting •
Topic 3.3: Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing, part of Writing 3.2 Guided Writing: Neatness and Legibility (2 Sessions) • Handwriting • in Grade 8 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: How can you improve your writing skills in Arabic?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify vocabulary related to the theme from a given text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write a simple paragraph on the theme for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. develop interest in writing Arabic.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify vocabulary related to the theme from a given text,

   Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. write a simple paragraph on the theme for effective communication,

   Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. develop interest in writing Arabic.

   Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work with peers to pick out words related to their surrounding from a given display,

2. work jointly to build a vocabulary bank based on the theme,

3. collaborate with peers to play scrabble games forming simple words related to the theme,

4. construct sentences using vocabulary on the theme,

5. reorganise jumbled up sentences to form a coherent and neatly written paragraph based on the theme.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers to pick out words related to their surrounding from a given display,
2. work jointly to build a vocabulary bank based on the theme,
3. collaborate with peers to play scrabble games forming simple words related to the theme,
4. construct sentences using vocabulary on the theme,
5. reorganise jumbled up sentences to form a coherent and neatly written paragraph based on the theme.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and Problem solving: These are enhanced as the learner analyses concepts by logical reasoning when

reorganising jumbled up sentences to form a coherent and neatly written paragraph.

• Creativity and Imagination: These are enhanced as the learner exchanges new ideas that inspire creativity when playing

scrabble games forming simple words related to the theme.
